meta.title: CANScope canonical pin ledger
meta.rule: This file is the single source of truth for every physical wire. The Rev 2 manual, every wiring diagram, the video storyboard/narration and the wire coverage checklist are generated from it by tools/hwdocs. Edit this file, never the generated outputs.
meta.physical_inspection: NONE. No board, module or wire has been physically inspected or measured by Claude. Every status below is based on documents and repository source only.

status_legend.CONFIRMED: Design value supported by a named datasheet or repository source AND it depends on no unidentified physical part. Still check both ends against the printed labels before wiring.
status_legend.PROVISIONAL: Design is supported by documents, but depends on a physical detail that only the builder can see. Wire it ONLY after every gate listed for it has passed and been recorded in the sign-off sheet.
status_legend.BLOCKED: Do NOT wire. Required information is missing. Supply the named evidence so the ledger can be updated first.

evidence.E-TI: Texas Instruments SN65HVD23x datasheet SLOS346O (rev. April 2018): pin 1 D (TXD input), 2 GND, 3 VCC (3.0-3.6 V recommended, 6 V abs max), 4 R (RXD output), 5 Vref, 6 CANL, 7 CANH, 8 Rs. Rs strong pull-down = high-speed, 10-100 kOhm to GND = slope control, >=0.75 VCC = standby (driver OFF, receiver listen-only). D/R abs max VCC + 0.5 V. ICC 10 mA typ / 17 mA max. Package marking VP230.
evidence.E-ESP32: Espressif ESP32 Series datasheet: strapping pins GPIO0, GPIO2, GPIO5, MTDI (GPIO12), MTDO (GPIO15); GPIO34-39 input-only with no internal pull-ups; internal pull-up about 45 kOhm.
evidence.E-WROOM: Espressif ESP32-WROOM-32 datasheet v3.8: GPIO6-11 connected to the integrated SPI flash (do not use); IO16 (module pin 27) and IO17 (module pin 28) are ordinary GPIOs on WROOM-32 (they are PSRAM pins only on WROVER modules).
evidence.E-ARD: framework-arduinoespressif32, variants/esp32/pins_arduino.h (installed in C:/canscope-pio): SDA = 21, SCL = 22 (Wire default pins for board esp32dev); TX = 1, RX = 3 (USB serial UART0).
evidence.E-FW: Repository firmware: firmware/node1/include/node1_hw_config.h, firmware/node2/include/node2_hw_config.h and firmware/monitor/include/monitor_hw_config.h set CAN TX GPIO17, RX GPIO16, 500 kbit/s; sketch_node1_test.ino and sketch_node2_test.ino use the same. firmware/node3 refuses to start CAN (all values UNVERIFIED).
evidence.E-DOIT: Widely published DOIT ESP32 DevKit V1 30-pin silkscreen order. This is NOT a manufacturer schematic: clone boards vary, so gate G2 compares it with the builder's board.
evidence.E-CALC: Hand calculation recorded in validation/correction_register.md (LED current, base drive, termination).

esp32_header.board: ESP32 DevKit V1, 30-pin, ESP-WROOM-32 (as stated by the user; not yet photographed)
esp32_header.orientation: Board viewed from the component side, USB connector pointing LEFT. Position 1 is the pin nearest the USB connector on each header.

G1.title: ESP32 module identity
G1.procedure: Read the laser marking on the metal shield of each ESP32. Photograph it.
G1.pass: It reads ESP32-WROOM-32 (or WROOM-32D/32E/32U). Not WROVER, not ESP32-S2/S3/C3.
G1.fail: STOP. GPIO16/17 may be PSRAM pins. Send the photo; the ledger must be revised.

G2.title: Header silkscreen matches the ledger
G2.procedure: With USB pointing left, read every pin label on both headers and compare with the 30-pin table (3V3 side: 3V3, GND, D15, D2, D4, RX2, TX2, D5, D18, D19, D21, RX0, TX0, D22, D23; VIN side: VIN, GND, D13, D12, D14, D27, D26, D25, D33, D32, D35, D34, VN, VP, EN).
G2.pass: All 30 labels match in the same order.
G2.fail: STOP. Do not count pins from the diagram. Send a photo of both headers.

G3.title: Breadboard fit
G3.procedure: Seat the ESP32 across the centre trench. Count free holes beside each pin row.
G3.pass: At least one free hole remains in the same 5-hole strip as every pin, on both sides.
G3.fail: Do not force it. Bridge the board across two breadboards (one header row in each) or use female-to-male jumpers on the header pins. Record which.

G4.title: Transceiver module identity and labels
G4.procedure: Read the 8-pin IC marking (expect VP230) and every printed pin label. Check whether the module has any 5 V pin or a voltage regulator. Photograph front and back.
G4.pass: IC reads VP230; supply pin is labelled 3V3/3.3V/VCC with no 5 V-only marking; you can find pins equivalent to 3V3, GND, CTX (TXD/D), CRX (RXD/R), CANH, CANL.
G4.fail: STOP. Different IC or a 5 V module needs a new design review.

G5.title: Transceiver Rs (mode) pin
G5.procedure: If the module exposes a pin labelled RS, S or STB: it must be wired to GND (see the conditional rows). If not exposed: with all power removed, measure resistance from IC pin 8 (Rs) to IC pin 2 (GND).
G5.pass: Exposed RS pin wired to GND, OR measured Rs-GND below 100 Ohm (high-speed mode per TI SLOS346O).
G5.fail: Rs-GND 10-100 kOhm (slope control) or open/high (standby, cannot transmit or ACK): STOP and record the value.

G6.title: Onboard termination
G6.procedure: With the module unpowered and NOT connected to anything, measure CANH to CANL on each transceiver module.
G6.pass: Reading above 10 kOhm (no onboard terminator) on all three modules: fit RT1 and RT2 exactly as the ledger says.
G6.fail: About 120 Ohm on a module: it has an onboard terminator. On TRX1/TRX3 omit the external RT1/RT2 at that node. On TRX2 (middle node): STOP, the onboard resistor must be removed or its jumper opened; send a photo first.

G7.title: OLED labels
G7.procedure: Read the four header labels left to right and the address marking on the back (0x78 = 0x3C, 0x7A = 0x3D).
G7.pass: Labels GND, VCC (or VDD), SCL (or SCK), SDA are present; record their order and address.
G7.fail: Different labels (e.g. SPI pins CS/DC/RES): STOP, it is not an I2C module.

G8.title: Push-button contacts
G8.procedure: Continuity mode: probe two diagonally opposite legs. Released: open. Pressed: beep / near 0 Ohm.
G8.pass: Diagonal legs are open when released and closed when pressed.
G8.fail: Rotate the meter probes to find a released-open / pressed-closed leg pair; record it and use it instead of the diagonal pair.

G9.title: LED polarity
G9.procedure: Long leg = anode (+). Flat edge on the rim = cathode (-). Confirm with the meter diode-test mode (red probe on anode lights the LED faintly).
G9.pass: Anode and cathode identified for every LED.
G9.fail: Legs cut equal and no flat edge visible: use diode test only.

G10.title: Transistor part and pinout
G10.procedure: Read the transistor marking. Look up E/B/C in that exact part's manufacturer datasheet. Common TO-92 examples (flat face toward you, legs down, left to right): PN2222A E-B-C; 2N3904 E-B-C; S8050 E-B-C; BC547 C-B-E. Your part may differ.
G10.pass: Part number and E/B/C order recorded from its own datasheet; Ic(max) >= 100 mA; NPN.

G11.title: Buzzer identity
G11.procedure: Confirm it is ACTIVE (sounds on plain DC), rated 5 V, current <= 30 mA, and find + (marked or longer leg). Note whether it is electromagnetic (needs flyback diode) or piezo.
G11.pass: Active 5 V, <= 30 mA, + identified, type recorded.
G11.fail: Passive buzzer, > 30 mA, or no polarity mark: STOP for design review.

G12.title: Node 3 VIN voltage
G12.when: First power-up of Node 3, buzzer + wire NOT installed
G12.procedure: Node 3 on USB only. Measure VIN to GND in DC volts.
G12.fail: Outside that range: do not install the buzzer supply wire; record value.

G13.title: Resistor values
G13.procedure: Measure every resistor out of circuit.

G14.title: Breadboard rails
G14.procedure: Continuity from one end of each rail to the other.
G14.pass: Continuous end to end, or the split point is marked.
G14.fail: Split rail: add a short bridge jumper on the same rail only, or keep loads on one half.

firmware_gaps: No firmware drives the OLED, LEDs, buttons or buzzer (GPIO21/22/25/26/27/32/33/18 are not referenced anywhere in firmware/).
No motor (RPM/temperature) or battery (voltage/current/SoC) simulation and no fault injection exist in the current node1/node2 targets; they only start CAN with TX disabled.
Only sketch_node2_test (PlatformIO env node2/legacy_sketch) transmits: fixed test frames 0x201, 0x202, 0x203 every 1 s and heartbeat 0x210 every 500 ms, UNVERIFIED units.
firmware/node3 refuses to start CAN by design. Node 3 hardware (the CANScope monitor) must run the firmware/monitor target, which is listen-only on GPIO17/16 at 500 kbit/s.

bus.bitrate_status: Firmware setting (E-FW); used consistently by node1, node2 legacy sketch and monitor. Not a production-bus value.
